extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / readers of Mochizuki's IUT series
extracted.subtask_short: proof/analysis of Corollary 3.12 in IUT III
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the logical/technical conditions and structural properties used in the proof of Corollary 3.12 (steps involving Θ-/q-pilot objects, multiradial constructions, log-Kummer correspondences, and log-volume comparisons) in Mochizuki's Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminacy (Ind1)
rubrics_metrics.description: May be thought of as arising from the requirement of compatibility with the permutation symmetries of the étale-picture (Theorem 3.11, (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indeterminacy is one of the formal 'quotient' type data to which the multiradial representation is subject; constructions (e.g., multiradial outputs, log-volumes) must be invariant or otherwise account for (Ind1). See Theorem 3.11, (i) and surrounding discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminacy (Ind2)
rubrics_metrics.description: May be thought of as arising from the requirement of compatibility with the AutF_{(cid:3)}×μ(−)-indeterminacies that act on the main/codomain of the Θ ×μ LGP-link with the horizontal arrows of the log-theta-lattice (Theorem 3.11, (i),(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructions must either be invariant under or control the effects of (Ind2); the procession-normalized log-volumes are designed to be invariant with respect to (Ind2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminacy (Ind3)
rubrics_metrics.description: May be thought of as arising from the requirement of compatibility with the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11, (ii), i.e., with the vertical arrows of the log-theta-lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Ind3) is converted into an inequality from above by taking suitable averages/log-volumes; constructions must accommodate the 'upper semi-compatibility' that (Ind3) represents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with a single Θ ×μ LGP-link
rubrics_metrics.description: To relate simultaneously both the unit and the value group portions on the 0-column to the 1-column one must concentrate on a single Θ ×μ LGP-link because the non-commutativity of the log-theta-lattice makes separate links impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof strategy chooses one LGP-link (e.g., from (0,0) to (1,0)) to compare unit and value-group data simultaneously and then applies bi-coricity; attempts to use two different LGP-links for units and value groups fail because of non-commutativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coricity of units (Theorem 1.5 (iii),(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the bi-coricity of the units to compute the 0-column Θ-pilot object in terms of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of the 1-column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mono-analytic log-shell interpretation of bi-coricity (Theorem 1.5 (iv)) to regard mono-analytic log-shells as multiradial mono-analytic containers for value-group structures; this is a central step in relating units across columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical coric invariance / vertically coric structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Work on the 0-column with structures invariant with respect to vertical shifts (i.e., (0,m)→(0,m+1)) such as vertically coric structures (indexed by '(n,◦)') that relate to non-vertically-coric 'Frobenius-like' structures via log-Kummer correspondences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This choice resolves the 'vertical shift vs impossibility of vertical shift' tension discussed in (iii),(iv) at the expense of admitting the upper semi-compatibility indeterminacy (Ind3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic-container requirement dichotomy (theta vs κ-coric)
rubrics_metrics.description: ´etale theta function / mono-theta environments require mono-analytic containers and have Kummer-theory behaviour incompatible with (Ind1),(Ind2); κ-coric functions are independent of mono-analytic containers and have Kummer theory compatible with (Ind1),(Ind2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish which kind of objects (theta-related or number-field-related/κ-coric) are in play, since this affects which compatibilities/indeterminacies arise (see Fig. 3.6 and Remarks 2.3.2–2.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer-detachment via log-Kummer correspondences
rubrics_metrics.description: Theory of 'Kummer-detachment' (Theorem 3.11, (ii),(iii)) allows relating Frobenioid-theoretic ('Frobenius-like') structures at the domain (0,0) to the multiradial representation, but only at the cost of introducing (Ind1),(Ind2),(Ind3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The log-Kummer correspondences are used to pass between vertically coric versions and other structures; accept and manage the resulting indeterminacies when applying this device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volumes invariance
rubrics_metrics.description: The procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volumes (averages over j∈F_l) furnish log-volumes ∈ R that are invariant with respect to the indeterminacies (Ind1) and (Ind2), and convert (Ind3) into an inequality from above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these normalized log-volumes to form a 'coarse space' or inductive limit that neutralizes certain formal-quotient indeterminacies and allows meaningful inequalities to be stated/proved (Proposition 3.9, Theorem 3.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-link compatibility of log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-link compatibility of the various log-volumes ensures they are compatible with the arrows (Kummer isomorphisms and log-links) of the log-Kummer correspondence of Theorem 3.11, (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing log-volumes across constructions, verify log-link compatibility (Proposition 3.9 (iv); final portion of Theorem 3.11 (ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial construction algorithm properties (IPL, SHE, APT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiradial construction algorithm of Theorem 3.11 yields outputs that satisfy (IPL) input prime-strip link, (SHE) simultaneous holomorphic expressibility, and (APT) algorithmic parallel transport properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the proof these properties are taken as logical constraints on the algorithm's input-output behaviour; one may 'temporarily forget' hidden internal structures but must preserve IPL, SHE, and APT to obtain the desired consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input prime-strip link (IPL) specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: The F_{(4)(5)}-prime-strip portion of the link/relationship consists precisely of (full poly-)isomorphisms of F_{(4)(5)}-prime-strips; the F_{(3)}×μ-prime-strip portion is more complicated due to indeterminacies (Ind1),(Ind2),(Ind3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting that output possibilities are linked to input prime-strips, specify which prime-strip types admit full-isomorphism links and which are affected by indeterminacies; this controls how concretely one can identify outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous Holomorphic Expressibility (SHE) — fixed pilot-object log-volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressibility relative to the arithmetic holomorphic structure in the 1-column means expressibility via operations valid even when the pilot-object log-volume associated to the input prime-strip is fixed to the value −|log(q)| ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SHE requires that constructions/operators used to realize output data remain well-defined under the constraint that the pilot-object log-volume equals −|log(q)|; use this to link input and output log-volumes (xi-e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic hull formation and log-volume comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Form the holomorphic hull 1,◦U (⊇ 1,◦U) of outputs and apply the log-volume to compare determinants of localizations of arithmetic vector bundles with the q-pilot object's log-volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlarge outputs to holomorphic hulls so they are expressed as localizations of arithmetic vector bundles over rings of the 1-column; then take determinants and apply normalized log-volumes to obtain comparable real-valued invariants (xi-d, xi-e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of determinants and normalized (j-averaged) log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: To compare rank>1 localizations to q-pilot objects (line-bundle objects) one must form suitable positive tensor powers, take determinants of arithmetic vector bundles, and apply the suitably normalized (with respect to j∈|F_l|) log-volume to regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives comparable log-volumes (e.g., −|log(Θ)| and −|log(q)|) and is necessary for the inequality conclusions (see Remark 3.9.5 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use global realized Frobenioids (not only local) for log-volume computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Global realized Frobenioids are essential because isomorphisms arising from the Θ ×μ LGP-link only preserve isomorphism classes of objects; local Frobenioids admit endomorphisms which are not automorphisms, causing indeterminacy in precise log-volume calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For precise log-volume computation and to avoid indeterminacies (e.g., p_v^N-multiples ambiguity), work at the global Frobenioid level (F_mod, F_R_MOD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity approach selection criteria (Fig. 3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate approaches to cyclotomic rigidity by their uni-/multi-radiality and compatibility with F_2^±-symmetry, profinite/tempered topologies, ring structures, and the log-link: e.g., mono-theta environments, MLF-Galois pairs (via Brauer groups), number-field algorithms (Q^>0 with (Z^×)=1) have differing compatibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the approach whose compatibility profile matches the structural requirements of the setting (e.g., ring-structure preservation, multiradial formulation) as summarized in Fig. 3.7 and the surrounding discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate synchronization via F_2^±-symmetry (necessity for bi-coricity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The constructions underlying the bi-coricity theory depend essentially on the conjugate synchronization arising from the F_2^±-symmetry, which relates local monoids and Galois groups at distinct labels while being compatible with vertically coric structures and distinguishing data indexed by distinct labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This synchronization is incompatible with the F_3^l-symmetry and therefore the two symmetries must be handled separately; verify compatibility conditions when using conjugate synchronization (see (vii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Kummer-tower procedures incompatible with ring structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms should be manifestly compatible with the topology of the profinite groups involved and should not require passing to Kummer towers, since Kummer towers are fundamentally incompatible with the ring structure of the fields involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer methods (e.g., those based on Galois cohomology of subquotients) that respect profinite/tempered topologies and ring structures (discussion in (vi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: N-th tensor power log-volume scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-volume of an N-th tensor power of a Θ-pilot object is computed by multiplying the log-volume of the original Θ-pilot object by N; the EtTh theory does not generalize evidently to N ≥ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume stronger inequalities obtainable by naive generalization; for N ≥ 2 the discrete rigidity and other ingredients prevent straightforward extension (xi-h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalized Θ LGP-links exponent λ inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: For generalized Θ ×μ LGP-links of the form q^λ→q (λ∈Q>0), the same arguments yield the inequality C_Θ ≥ −λ (sharper when λ<1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raising to the λ-th power on one side is not symmetric with respect to other sides; such generalized links can be treated by the same overall method to deduce modified inequalities (Remark 3.12.1 (ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish arithmetic holomorphic structures to identify intertwining
rubrics_metrics.description: Which intertwining between value-group and unit-group portions one considers (i.e., which arithmetic holomorphic structure) determines which log-volume an abstract prime-strip corresponds to; treating prime-strips only up to isomorphism makes Θ- and q-pilot objects 'indistinguishable' without fixing structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the arithmetic holomorphic structures chosen in domain and codomain of the Θ ×μ LGP-link: different choices lead to different identifications/intertwinings and hence different log-volume assignments (xi and (bitw)/(aitw)/(citw) discussion).
